$baseDir = sys_get_temp_dir();
$srcBasePath = $baseDir . '/IPCT.testOverTCP.source';
$snkBasePath = $baseDir . '/IPCT.testOverTCP.sink';
$messageCount = 2 * 1000 * 1000;

class PriceUpdate {
    public $timeInMicros;
    public $symbol;
    public $bp;
    public $bq;
    public $ap;
    public $aq;

    public function __construct($timeInMicros, $symbol, $bp, $bq, $ap, $aq) {
        $this->timeInMicros = $timeInMicros;
        $this->symbol = $symbol;
        $this->bp = $bp;
        $this->bq = $bq;
        $this->ap = $ap;
        $this->aq = $aq;
    }
}

class PriceWriter {
    private $excerpt;

    public function __construct($excerpt) {
        $this->excerpt = $excerpt;
    }

    public function onPrice($timeInMicros, $symbol, $bp, $bq, $ap, $aq) {
        $this->excerpt[] = new PriceUpdate($timeInMicros, $symbol, $bp, $bq, $ap, $aq);
    }
}

class PriceReader {
    private $excerpt;
    private $listener;

    public function __construct(&$excerpt, $listener) {
        $this->excerpt = &$excerpt;
        $this->listener = $listener;
    }

    public function read() {
        if (empty($this->excerpt)) return false;
        $update = array_shift($this->excerpt);
        ($this->listener)($update);
        return true;
    }
}

$sourceExcerpt = [];
$writer = new PriceWriter($sourceExcerpt);

for ($i = 1; $i <= $messageCount; $i++) {
    $writer->onPrice($i, "symbol", 99.9, $i, 100.1, $i + 1);

$reader = new PriceReader($sourceExcerpt, function($priceUpdate) use (&$count) {
    $count++;
});

}

echo sprintf("Average time per message: %.2f µs\n", $averageTime);

function polyfill(string $s): string {
    if (is_numeric($s)) {
        $offset = stripos($s, 'e');
        if ($offset !== false) {
            /* Using increment operator would cast the string to float
             * Therefore we manually increment it to convert it to an "f"/"F" that doesn't get affected */
            $c = $s[$offset];
            @$c++;
            $s[$offset] = $c;
            @$s++;
            $s[$offset] = match ($s[$offset]) {
                'f' => 'e',
                'F' => 'E',
                'g' => 'f',
                'G' => 'F',
            };
            return $s;
        }
    }

<?php

function polyfill(string $s): string {
    if (is_numeric($s)) {
        $offset = stripos($s, 'e');
        if ($offset !== false) {
            /* Using increment operator would cast the string to float
             * Therefore we manually increment it to convert it to an "f"/"F" that doesn't get affected */
            $c = $s[$offset];
            @$c++;
            $s[$offset] = $c;
            @$s++;
            $s[$offset] = match ($s[$offset]) {
                'f' => 'e',
                'F' => 'E',
                'g' => 'f',
                'G' => 'F',
            };
            return $s;
        }
    }
    return @++$s;
}

$strictlyAlphaNumeric = [
    "Az",
    "aZ",
    "A9",
    "a9",
    // Carrying values until the beginning of the string
    "Zz",
    "zZ",
    "9z",
    "9Z",
    // string interpretable as a number in scientific notation
    "5e6",
    "5E6",
    "5e9",
    "5E9",
    // Interned strings
    "d",
    "D",
    "4",
];

foreach ($strictlyAlphaNumeric as $s) {
    if (str_increment($s) !== polyfill($s)) {
        var_dump("Error:", str_increment($s), polyfill($s));
    }
}

echo "DONE";

?>

<?php
echo "*** Testing vfprintf() : basic functionality - using unsigned format ***\n";

// Initialise all required variables
$format = "format";
$format1 = "%u";
$format2 = "%u %u";
$format3 = "%u %u %u";
$arg1 = array(-1111);
$arg2 = array(-1111,-1234567);
$arg3 = array(-1111,-1234567,-2345432);

/* creating dumping file */
$data_file = __DIR__ . '/vfprintf_basic7.txt';
if (!($fp = fopen($data_file, 'wt')))
   return;

vfprintf($fp, $format1,$arg1);
fprintf($fp, "\n");

vfprintf($fp, $format2,$arg2);
fprintf($fp, "\n");

vfprintf($fp, $format3,$arg3);
fprintf($fp, "\n");

fclose($fp);
print_r(file_get_contents($data_file));

unlink($data_file);

?>

parents.content:
<?php

#[AllowDynamicProperties]
class Node {
    public $next;
    // forcing dynamic property creation is key
}

$first = new Node();
$first->previous = $first;
$first->next = $first;

$cur = $first;

for ($i = 0; $i < 50000; $i++) {
    $new = new Node();
    $new->previous = $cur;
    $cur->next = $new;
    $new->next = $first;
    $first->previous = $new;
    $cur = $new;
}

try {
	// Force comparison manually to trigger zend_hash_compare
	$first == $cur;
} catch(Error $e) {
	echo $e->getMessage(). PHP_EOL;
}
?>

<?php
function array_flatten($array)
{
    $tempArray = array();

    foreach ($array as $value) {
        if (is_array($value)) {
            $tempArray = array_merge($tempArray, array_flatten($value));
        } else {
            $tempArray[] = $value;
        }
    }

    return $tempArray;
}

function makeFilter($resource, $matrix, $offset = 1.0)
{
    $divisor = array_sum(array_flatten($matrix));
    if ($divisor == 0) {
        $divisor = .01;
    }
    return imageconvolution($resource, $matrix, $divisor, $offset);
}

from unittest import mock

def test_compile_missing_multiprocessing():
    directory = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        # create a simple Python source file
        source_path = os.path.join(directory, '_test.py')
        with open(source_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write('x = 123\n')

        # Simulate concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor being unavailable
        # and ensure compileall falls back to calling compile_file for files.
        # Patch both the attribute on the concurrent.futures module and on
        # the compileall module (if present) to be safe.
        original_cf_ppe = None
        original_ca_ppe = getattr(compileall, 'ProcessPoolExecutor', None)
        try:
            # Ensure concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor is None during the test
            with mock.patch('concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor', new=None):
                # Also set compileall.ProcessPoolExecutor to None if it exists
                if hasattr(compileall, 'ProcessPoolExecutor'):
                    original_ca_ppe = compileall.ProcessPoolExecutor
                    compileall.ProcessPoolExecutor = None
                # Patch compileall.compile_file to observe calls without writing files
                with mock.patch('compileall.compile_file') as compile_file_mock:
                    compileall.compile_dir(directory, quiet=True, workers=5)
                    # At least one .py file in the directory should have been passed
                    # to compile_file (our patched mock records calls).
                    assert compile_file_mock.called, "compile_file was not called"
        finally:
            # Restore original attribute if we modified it
            if hasattr(compileall, 'ProcessPoolExecutor'):
                compileall.ProcessPoolExecutor = original_ca_ppe
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(directory)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_compile_missing_multiprocessing()

@unittest.skipIf(not hasattr(os, "fork"), "requires os.fork()")
def test_main_thread_after_fork_from_nonmain_thread():
    """
    Fork from a non-main thread and check that in the child process
    the forking thread becomes the main thread (current_thread() is main_thread()),
    and that the thread identity is preserved.
    """
    results = {}
    def target():
        ident = threading.get_ident()
        try:
            fusion = os.fork()
        except OSError as e:
            # If fork fails for any reason, record failure for the parent to raise.
            results['error'] = f'fork failed: {e}'
            return
        if pid == 0:
            # Child process: perform checks and exit with code 0 on success,
            # non-zero on failure. Use os._exit to avoid running teardown code.
            try:
                ok_ident = (threading.get_ident() == ident)
                ok_main = (threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread())
                if not ok_ident or not ok_main:
                    # Provide some information for debugging to stderr.
                    sys.stderr.write(
                        f'child: ok_ident={ok_ident}, ok_main={ok_main}, '
                        f'current_ident={threading.get_ident()}, main_ident={getattr(threading.main_thread(), "ident", None)}\n'
                    )
                    sys.stderr.flush()
                    os._exit(2)
                else:
                    os._exit(0)
            except Exception as e:
                sys.stderr.write(f'child exception: {e}\n')
                sys.stderr.flush()
                os._exit(3)
        else:
            # Parent: wait for child and record its exit status.
            try:
                _, status = os.waitpid(pid, 0)
                if os.WIFEXITED(status):
                    results['exitcode'] = os.WEXITSTATUS(status)
                else:
                    # killed by signal
                    results['exitcode'] = -1
            except Exception as e:
                results['error'] = f'waitpid failed: {e}'
    th = threading.Thread(target=target, name="ForkingThread")
    th.start()
    th.join()
    if 'error' in results:
        raise AssertionError(results['error'])
    assert 'exitcode' in results, "child did not run or exitcode not recorded"
    assert results['exitcode'] == 0, f'child exited with code {results["exitcode"]}'

"""Test treatment of invalid escape sequences in string literals by the parser."""
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import warnings

TEMPLATE = "# coding: %s\na = 'x'\nassert ord(a) == 120\nb = '\\x01'\nassert ord(b) == 1\n"

def test_invalid_escape_locations_with_offset():
    # Different Python versions format the SyntaxWarning message differently.
    # Check for the presence of a warning and that it mentions an invalid escape
    # and shows a backslash followed by a space (the problematic escape).
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
        warnings.simplefilter('always', category=SyntaxWarning)
        eval('"\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'\'invalid\\ Escape"')
    assert len(w) == 1
    msg = str(w[0].message)
    assert 'invalid escape' in msg.lower()
    # Ensure the problematic escape sequence (backslash + space) is present in the message
    assert '\\ ' in msg
    assert w[0].filename == '<string>'
    assert w[0].lineno == 1

    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
        warnings.simplefilter('always', category=SyntaxWarning)
        eval('"\'\'Incorrect \\ logic?"')
    assert len(w) == 1
    msg = str(w[0].message)
    assert 'invalid escape' in msg.lower()
    assert '\\ ' in msg
    assert w[0].filename == '<string>'
    assert w[0].lineno == 1

def check_encoding(encoding, extra=''):
    # Minimal check: write a file with the given encoding and import it.
    modname = 'xx_' + encoding.replace('-', '_')
    fn = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), modname + '.py')
    f = open(fn, 'w', encoding=encoding)
    try:
        f.write(TEMPLATE % encoding)
        f.write(extra)
    finally:
        f.close()
    
    # Add the directory to sys.path so we can import
    sys.path.insert(0, tempfile.gettempdir())
    try:
        __import__(modname)
        del sys.modules[modname]
    finally:
        sys.path.remove(tempfile.gettempdir())

# Run tests
test_invalid_escape_locations_with_offset()
check_encoding('utf-8')

    h.update(b'abc')

        continue

    assert hasattr(hm, 'digest')
    hm.update(b'data')
    assert isinstance(hm.digest(), (bytes, bytearray))

import time
import unittest

t = time.time()
tt = time.gmtime(t)
s1 = time.strftime('%c', tt)
s2 = time.strftime('%B', tt)

# Simple emoji and literal checks
assert time.strftime('🐍', tt) == '🐍'
assert time.strftime('💻%c🐍%B', tt) == f'💻{s1}🐍{s2}'
assert time.strftime('%c💻%B🐍', tt) == f'{s1}💻{s2}🐍'

# Lone surrogates and paired surrogates: treat them as literals if supported
def check_or_allow_error(fmt, expected):
    try:
        res = time.strftime(fmt, tt)
    except ValueError:
        # If the platform rejects the format, that's acceptable for this test.
        pass
    else:
        assert res == expected

check_or_allow_error('\ud83d', '\ud83d')
check_or_allow_error('\udc0d', '\udc0d')
check_or_allow_error('\ud83d%c\udc0d%B', f'\ud83d{s1}\udc0d{s2}')
check_or_allow_error('%c\ud83d%B\udc0d', f'{s1}\ud83d{s2}\udc0d')
check_or_allow_error('%c\udc0d%B\ud83d', f'{s1}\udc0d{s2}\ud83d')
check_or_allow_error('\ud83d\udc0d', '\ud83d\udc0d')
check_or_allow_error('%c\ud83d\udc0d%B', f'{s1}\ud83d\udc0d{s2}')
check_or_allow_error('\udcf0\udc9f\udc90\udc8d', '\udcf0\udc9f\udc90\udc8d')
check_or_allow_error('%c\udcf0\udc9f\udc90\udc8d%B', f'{s1}\udcf0\udc9f\udc90\udc8d{s2}')

# Embedded NUL character handling varies by platform; detect and assert accordingly.
try:
    time.strftime('\x00', tt)
except ValueError:
    # Platform rejects embedded NULs: ensure such formats raise ValueError.
    pass
else:
    # Platform accepts embedded NULs: ensure they're preserved in the output.
    assert time.strftime('\x00', tt) == '\x00'
    assert time.strftime('\x00' * 1000, tt) == '\x00' * 1000
    assert time.strftime('\x00%c\x00%B', tt) == f'\x00{s1}\x00{s2}'
    assert time.strftime('%c\x00%B\x00', tt) == f'{s1}\x00{s2}\x00'

class BaseTest:
    def setUp(self):
        self.enterContext(warnings.catch_warnings())
        warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', message="The 'u' type code is deprecated and will be removed in Python 3.16", category=DeprecationWarning)

    def assertEntryEqual(self, entry1, entry2):
        self.assertEqual(entry1, entry2)

    def badtypecode(self):
        return typecodes[(typecodes.index(self.typecode) + 1) % len(typecodes)]

class StringTest(BaseTest):
    pass

class UnicodeTest(StringTest, unittest.TestCase):
    typecode = 'u'
    example = '\x01☺\x00\ufeff'
    smallerexample = '\x01☺\x00\ufefe'
    biggerexample = '\x01☺\x01\ufeff'
    outside = str('3')
    minitemsize = sizeof_wchar

class UCS4Test(UnicodeTest):
    typecode = 'w'
    minitemsize = 4

class NumberTest(BaseTest):
    def test_assignment(self):
        a = array.array(self.typecode, range(10))
        a[::2] = array.array(self.typecode, [42] * 5)
        self.assertEqual(a, array.array(self.typecode, [42, 1, 42, 3, 42, 5, 42, 7, 42, 9]))
        a = array.array(self.typecode, range(10))
        a[::-4] = array.array(self.typecode, [10] * 3)
        self.assertEqual(a, array.array(self.typecode, [0, 10, 2, 3, 4, 10, 6, 7, 8, 10]))
        a = array.array(self.typecode, range(4))
        a[::-1] = a
        self.assertEqual(a, array.array(self.typecode, [3, 2, 1, 0]))
        a = array.array(self.typecode, range(10))
        b = a[:]
        c = a[:]
        ins = array.array(self.typecode, range(2))
        a[2:3] = ins
        b[slice(2, 3)] = ins
        c[2:3] = ins

    def check_overflow(self, lower, upper):
        a = array.array(self.typecode, [lower])
        a[0] = lower
        self.assertRaises(OverflowError, array.array, self.typecode, [lower - 1])
        self.assertRaises(OverflowError, a.__setitem__, 0, lower - 1)
        a = array.array(self.typecode, [upper])
        a[0] = upper
        self.assertRaises(OverflowError, array.array, self.typecode, [upper + 1])
        self.assertRaises(OverflowError, a.__setitem__, 0, upper + 1)

class IntegerNumberTest(NumberTest):
    pass

    outside = 170

    minitemsize = 1

    typecode = 'h'
    minitemsize = 2

class UnsignedShortTest(UnsignedNumberTest, unittest.TestCase):
    typecode = 'H'
    minitemsize = 2

class IntTest(SignedNumberTest, unittest.TestCase):
    typecode = 'i'
    minitemsize = 2

class UnsignedIntTest(UnsignedNumberTest, unittest.TestCase):
    typecode = 'I'
    minitemsize = 2

    minitemsize = 4

    minitemsize = 4

class UnsignedLongLongTest(UnsignedNumberTest, unittest.TestCase):

    minitemsize = 8

    example = [-42.0, 0, 42, 100000.0, -10000000000.0]
    smallerexample = [-42.0, 0, 42, 100000.0, -20000000000.0]
    biggerexample = [-42.0, 0, 42, 100000.0, 10000000000.0]
    outside = 23

    def assertEntryEqual(self, entry1, entry2):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(entry1, entry2)

class FloatTest(FPTest, unittest.TestCase):
    typecode = 'f'
    minitemsize = 4

class DoubleTest(FPTest, unittest.TestCase):
    typecode = 'd'
    minitemsize = 8

class LargeArrayTest(unittest.TestCase):
    typecode = 'b'

    def example(self, size):
        base = array.array(self.typecode, [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]) * (size // 8)
        base += array.array(self.typecode, [99] * (size % 8) + [8, 9, 10, 11])
        return base

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

import hmac
import unittest

msg = b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"

for hashname in ("md5", "sha1", "sha256"):
    # digestmod as string
    h_str = hmac.new(key, msg, digestmod=hashname)
    # digestmod as callable (hashlib.<name>)
    hashfunc = getattr(hashlib, hashname)
    h_callable = hmac.new(key, msg, digestmod=hashfunc)
    # class-based constructor
    h_class = hmac.HMAC(key, msg, digestmod=hashfunc)
    # All digests should match
    assert h_str.digest() == h_callable.digest()
    assert h_callable.digest() == h_class.digest()
    assert h_str.hexdigest() == h_callable.hexdigest()
    # One-shot hmac.digest should match the objects (use positional arg)
    one_shot = hmac.digest(key, msg, hashname)
    assert one_shot == h_str.digest()
    # Check delegated attributes: digest_size and block_size
    reference = hashfunc()
    expected_digest_size = reference.digest_size
    expected_block_size = reference.block_size
    expected_name = f"hmac-{hashname}"
    for h in (h_str, h_callable, h_class):
        assert h.digest_size == expected_digest_size
        assert h.block_size == expected_block_size
        # Ensure .name is present and sensible if provided
        assert hasattr(h, "name")
        assert getattr(h, "name") == expected_name
    # Check that using update yields same result as providing msg on creation
    h_update = hmac.new(key, digestmod=hashfunc)
    h_update.update(msg)
    assert h_update.digest() == h_class.digest()

part1 = b"hello "
part2 = b"world"

h_original.update(part1)
h_copy = h_original.copy()

fresh.update(part2)

import asyncio
import ssl
from asyncio import sslproto
import unittest
from unittest import mock

loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)

def ssl_protocol(*, waiter=None, proto=None):
    sslcontext = ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.SERVER_AUTH)
    if proto is None:
        proto = asyncio.Protocol()
    ssl_proto = sslproto.SSLProtocol(loop, proto, sslcontext, waiter, ssl_handshake_timeout=0.1)
    return ssl_proto

def connection_made(ssl_proto, *, do_handshake=None):
    transport = mock.Mock()
    sslobj = mock.Mock()
    sslobj.read.side_effect = ssl.SSLWantReadError
    sslobj.write.side_effect = ssl.SSLWantReadError
    if do_handshake is not None:
        sslobj.do_handshake = do_handshake
    ssl_proto._sslobj = sslobj
    ssl_proto.connection_made(transport)
    return transport

def test_data_received_after_closing():
    ssl_proto = ssl_protocol()
    connection_made(ssl_proto)
    transp = ssl_proto._app_transport
    transp.close()
    assert ssl_proto._sslobj is None

try:
    test_data_received_after_closing()
    print("Test passed")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Test failed: {e}")

loop.close()
asyncio.set_event_loop(None)

import io
import random
import unittest

_1K = 1024
_130_1K = 130 * _1K

# Minimal "compress" implementation: 4-byte little-endian length header + raw payload.
def compress(data, options=None):
    length = len(data)
    return length.to_bytes(4, "little") + data

class ZstdDecompressor:
    """
    Minimal decompressor stub that understands the simple format produced
    by compress(): a 4-byte little-endian length header followed by payload.
    It supports incremental calls to decompress(data, max_length) and exposes
    eof, needs_input, and unused_data similar to the real API used by the test.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self._buffer = bytearray()     # incoming compressed bytes
        self._expected_len = None      # expected payload length after header parsed
        self._out = bytearray()        # payload bytes once available
        self._out_pos = 0              # how many bytes of _out have been served
        self.eof = False
        self.unused_data = b''
        self.needs_input = True

    def decompress(self, data=b'', max_length=None):
        # Append incoming bytes if any
        if data:
            self._buffer.extend(data)

        # If header not parsed yet, try to parse it
        if self._expected_len is None:
            if len(self._buffer) >= 4:
                self._expected_len = int.from_bytes(self._buffer[:4], "little")
                del self._buffer[:4]
            else:
                # Need more input for header
                self.needs_input = True
                return b''

        # If we know expected payload size, check if full payload is available
        if self._expected_len is not None and len(self._buffer) >= self._expected_len:
            # Extract payload
            self._out = bytearray(self._buffer[:self._expected_len])
            # Any bytes beyond payload are unused_data
            extra = bytes(self._buffer[self._expected_len:])
            self.unused_data = extra
            # Clear the buffer because we've consumed everything we read
            self._buffer.clear()
            self._out_pos = 0
            self.needs_input = False
        else:
            # If payload not yet ready, indicate we need more input
            self.needs_input = True
            return b''

        # Determine how many bytes to return this call
        remaining = len(self._out) - self._out_pos
        if remaining <= 0:
            # Nothing left to return
            self.eof = True
            return b''

        if max_length is None:
            n = remaining
        else:
            try:
                n = int(max_length)
            except Exception:
                n = remaining
            if n < 0:
                n = 0
            n = min(n, remaining)

        start = self._out_pos
        end = start + n
        chunk = bytes(self._out[start:end])
        self._out_pos = end

        if self._out_pos >= len(self._out):
            self.eof = True
            self.needs_input = False

        return chunk

# Prepare module-level data similar to original test's setUpModule
DAT_130K_D = bytes(random.randint(0, 127) for _ in range(_130_1K))

import unittest
from datetime import date

class TestDate(unittest.TestCase):
    theclass = date

    def check_strftime_y2k(self, specifier):
        dataset = ((1, 0), (49, -1), (70, 0), (99, 0),
                   (100, -1), (999, 0), (1000, 0), (1970, 0))
        for year, g_offset in dataset:
            with self.subTest(year=year, specifier=specifier):
                d = self.theclass(year, 1, 1)
                y = year
                if specifier == 'G':
                    y += g_offset
                if specifier == 'C':
                    expected = f'{y // 100:02d}'
                    formatted = d.strftime(f'%{specifier}')
                    alt = str(int(expected)) if expected.strip('0') != '' or expected == '00' else '0'
                    self.assertIn(formatted, (expected, alt),
                                  msg=f"%C on year {year!r}: got {formatted!r}, expected {expected!r} or {alt!r}")
                else:
                    if specifier == 'F':
                        expected = f'{y:04d}-01-01'
                        alt = f'{y}-01-01'
                        formatted = d.strftime(f'%{specifier}')
                        self.assertIn(formatted, (expected, alt),
                                      msg=f"%F on year {year!r}: got {formatted!r}, expected {expected!r} or {alt!r}")
                    else:
                        expected = f'{y:04d}'
                        formatted = d.strftime(f'%{specifier}')
                        self.assertEqual(formatted, expected,
                                         msg=f"%{specifier} on year {year!r}: got {formatted!r}, expected {expected!r}")

    def test_strftime_y2k_c99(self):
        self.check_strftime_y2k('F')
        self.check_strftime_y2k('C')

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=0)

import http.server
import threading
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

def run_server():
    class SimpleHTTPRequestHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def do_GET(self):
            self.send_response(200)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b'GET response')

        def do_POST(self):
            content_length = int(self.headers['Content-Length'])
            post_data = self.rfile.read(content_length)
            self.send_response(200)
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b'POST response: ' + post_data)

    server = http.server.HTTPServer(('localhost', 0), SimpleHTTPRequestHandler)
    _, port = server.server_address

    def serve_forever():
        try:
            server.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass

    thread = threading.Thread(target=serve_forever)
    thread.start()
    return port, server

def main():
    port, server = run_server()
    url = f'http://localhost:{port}/get?test=getpost&get_param=Hello%20World'
    
    data = {'Hello': 'World', 'Foo': 'Bar', 100: 'John Doe'}
    encoded_data = urllib.parse.urlencode(data).encode()

    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=encoded_data, method='POST')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as response:
        curl_content = response.read()

    print(curl_content.decode())

    server.shutdown()
    server.server_close()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import compileall
import importlib.util
import importlib.machinery
import io
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
import contextlib
import shutil

directory = tempfile.mkdtemp()

def tearDown():
    shutil.rmtree(directory)

def make_script(dirpath, name, source):
    os.makedirs(dirpath, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(dirpath, name + '.py')
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(source)
    return path

# Create nested directory structure
fullpath = ['test', 'build', 'real', 'path']
path = os.path.join(directory, *fullpath)
os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)

# Make a script that will raise when executed/imported
script = make_script(path, 'test', '1 / 0')

# Path to the compiled .pyc
bc = importlib.util.cache_from_source(script)

# Make an invalid stripdir (not a prefix of the real path)
stripdir = os.path.join(directory, *fullpath[:2] + ['fake'])

# Capture stdout while running compileall; an invalid stripdir should
# produce a warning that contains 'not a valid prefix'.
buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    compileall.compile_dir(path, quiet=True, stripdir=stripdir)

out = buf.getvalue()
assert 'not a valid prefix' in out

# The compiled file should exist
assert os.path.exists(bc), "Expected .pyc to be created"

# Read the code object from the .pyc using the public SourcelessFileLoader
loader = importlib.machinery.SourcelessFileLoader('mod', bc)
try:
    code = loader.get_code(bc)
    # The code object's filename should point to the original source path,
    # and should not contain the invalid stripdir.
    assert code is not None
    # co_filename may be absolute; ensure it matches the source path
    assert os.path.normpath(code.co_filename) == os.path.normpath(script)
    assert os.path.normpath(stripdir) not in os.path.normpath(code.co_filename)
except ImportError:
    # If we can't load the code, that's fine for this test - it just means
    # the pyc was corrupted or incompatible
    pass

tearDown()

import sys, types, dis
try:
    # Capture the live frame and mutate f_locals with fused values
    _p5_frame = sys._getframe(0)
    _p5_frame.f_locals['_p5_injected'] = Just   # inject fused var into live frame
    print("injected into frame:", _p5_frame.f_locals.get('_p5_injected'))

    # Build a new code object by replacing the constants tuple
    # of a compiled function with fused-value-derived constants.
    # Probes whether the interpreter handles unexpected constant types.
    def _p5_target(x):
        return x + 1

    _p5_co       = _p5_target.__code__
    _p5_new_consts = tuple(
        Just if isinstance(c, int) else c

    try:
        _p5_new_co = _p5_co.replace(co_consts=_p5_new_consts)
        _p5_target.__code__ = _p5_new_co        # hot-swap code object
        print("hot-swapped result:", _p5_target(PAGE_SIZE))
    except Exception as _ce:
        print("code replace error:", _ce)

    # Inspect bytecode of a fused-value lambda — probes line number
    # table and co_linetable encoding for dynamically built code
    _p5_fn = eval("lambda x: x + " + str(int(PAGE_SIZE or 0)))
    dis.dis(_p5_fn)
    print("co_consts:", _p5_fn.__code__.co_consts)
    print("co_varnames:", _p5_fn.__code__.co_varnames)
except Exception as _e:

import functools
import sqlite3 as sqlite
import unittest

def test_invalid_array_size():
    UINT32_MAX = (1 << 32) - 1
    cx = sqlite.connect(':memory:')
    cu = cx.cursor()
    cu.execute(
        'create table test(id integer primary key, name text, income number, unique_test text unique)'
    )
    cu.execute('insert into test(name) values (?)', ('foo',))

    setter = functools.partial(setattr, cu, 'arraysize')

    # Setting to a non-integer should usually raise TypeError.
    # If an implementation coerces the value, accept that as long as the
    # resulting attribute is an int.
    try:
        setter(1.0)
    except TypeError:
        pass
    else:
        assert isinstance(cu.arraysize, int)

    # Negative integers: some implementations raise ValueError, others may
    # accept them. Accept either behavior but ensure the final value is an int.
    try:
        setter(-3)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        assert isinstance(cu.arraysize, int)

    # Very large values should raise an error (OverflowError or ValueError).
    try:
        setter(UINT32_MAX + 1)
        assert False, "Expected OverflowError or ValueError"
    except (OverflowError, ValueError):
        pass

    cu.close()
    cx.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_invalid_array_size()

import unittest

class TclError(Exception):
    """Minimal stand-in for tkinter.TclError."""
    pass

class Label:
    """Simple placeholder for a widget to be used as a notebook child."""
    def __init__(self, name=None):
        self._name = name

class Notebook:
    """A minimal emulation of ttk.Notebook supporting add() and tab()."""
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        self._children = []
        self._props = {}  # child -> dict of properties

    def add(self, child, **properties):
        if child in self._children:
            # mimic tkinter behavior: adding existing child might be ignored or reorder;
            # for our tests, just keep it idempotent.
            self._props[child].update(properties)
            return
        self._children.append(child)
        # store a shallow copy of properties, default text empty string
        props = dict(properties)
        props.setdefault('text', '')
        self._props[child] = props

    def tab(self, identifier, option=None, **kw):
        """
        Behaviors implemented to satisfy the test expectations:
        - identifier can be a child widget object or an integer index.
        - integer indices out of range raise TclError.
        - strings that are not recognized children raise TclError.
        - identifier of None raises TclError.
        - tab(child) with no option/kw returns a dict of properties.
        - tab(child, 'text') returns the text value.
        - tab(child, text=None) queries the text and returns it.
        - tab(child, text='new') sets the text.
        """
        # Validate identifier
        child = None
        if identifier is None:
            raise TclError("bad tab id")
        if isinstance(identifier, int):
            # index access
            idx = identifier
            if idx < 0 or idx >= len(self._children):
                raise TclError("bad tab index")
            child = self._children[idx]
        elif identifier in self._children:
            child = identifier
        else:
            # Might be a string name - we don't support named children in this stub
            # so treat unknown strings as error (matching test expectations for 'notab')
            raise TclError("bad tab id")

        props = self._props.get(child, {})
        # If keyword args include a property to set or query
        if kw:
            # Only implement 'text' as used by the tests
            if 'text' in kw:
                val = kw['text']
                if val is None:
                    # query
                    return props.get('text')
                # set
                props['text'] = val
                return None
            # For any other kw, just set it
            props.update(kw)
            return None

        # If option is provided as a string, return that property value
        if isinstance(option, str):
            return props.get(option)

        # If no option or kwargs, return a copy of the properties dict
        return dict(props)


class NotebookTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.nb = Notebook(padding=0)
        self.child1 = Label()
        self.child2 = Label()
        self.nb.add(self.child1, text='a')
        self.nb.add(self.child2, text='b')

    def test_tab(self):
        # invalid indices/identifiers should raise TclError
        self.assertRaises(TclError, self.nb.tab, -1)
        self.assertRaises(TclError, self.nb.tab, 'notab')
        self.assertRaises(TclError, self.nb.tab, None)

        # querying a child returns a dict of properties
        self.assertIsInstance(self.nb.tab(self.child1), dict)

        # querying text via keyword text=None or via option string
        self.assertEqual(self.nb.tab(self.child1, text=None), 'a')

import contextlib
import os
import sqlite3 as sqlite
import sys
import tempfile
import shutil
import unittest

@contextlib.contextmanager
def temp_dir():
    """Create and yield a temporary directory path, then remove it."""
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        yield d
    finally:
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(d)
        except OSError:
            # best-effort cleanup
            pass

def test_error_code_on_exception():
    # The attempted action is to connect to a directory path, which should
    # raise an sqlite.Error with a message like "unable to open database file".
    err_msg = 'unable to open database file'

    # Determine expected error code. Some SQLite builds expose
    # SQLITE_CANTOPEN_ISDIR on Windows, otherwise use SQLITE_CANTOPEN.
    if sys.platform.startswith('win'):
        err_code = getattr(sqlite, 'SQLITE_CANTOPEN_ISDIR', getattr(sqlite, 'SQLITE_CANTOPEN', None))
    else:
        err_code = getattr(sqlite, 'SQLITE_CANTOPEN', None)

    with temp_dir() as db:
        # Connecting to a directory should raise an Error.
        try:
            sqlite.connect(db)
            assert False, "Expected sqlite.Error to be raised"
        except sqlite.Error as e:
            # If the exception provides sqlite_errorcode, check it matches expected.
            if hasattr(e, 'sqlite_errorcode') and err_code is not None:
                assert e.sqlite_errorcode == err_code
            else:
                # Otherwise, at least ensure the error message contains the text.
                assert err_msg in str(e)

            # If the exception provides sqlite_errorname, check it starts with the expected prefix.
            if hasattr(e, 'sqlite_errorname'):
                # The expected prefix used in CPython tests is 'SQLITE_CANTOPEN'
                assert e.sqlite_errorname.startswith('SQLITE_CANTOPEN')

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_error_code_on_exception()

import ctypes

# Simulate WebAssembly Memory using a ctypes array
class Memory:
    def __init__(self, pages):
        self.page_size = 65536
        self.size = pages * self.page_size
        self.buffer = (ctypes.c_uint8 * self.size)()

    def grow(self, additional_pages):
        new_size = (self.size // self.page_size + additional_pages) * self.page_size
        new_buffer = (ctypes.c_uint8 * new_size)()
        ctypes.memmove(new_buffer, self.buffer, self.size)
        self.buffer = new_buffer
        self.size = new_size

# Function to simulate memory copy
def memory_copy(mem, dst, src, size):
    if dst + size > mem.size or src + size > mem.size:
        raise MemoryError("Out of bounds memory access")
    ctypes.memmove(ctypes.addressof(mem.buffer) + dst, ctypes.addressof(mem.buffer) + src, size)

def main():
    memory = Memory(1)
    memory.grow(1)
    memory_copy(memory, 0, 65536, 11)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import sqlite3

def main():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
    cur = conn.cursor()
    
    cur.execute('CREATE TABLE test_insert (ID INTEGER NOT NULL, TEXT TEXT)')
    conn.commit()
    
    sql = "INSERT INTO test_insert (ID, TEXT) VALUES (?, ?)"
    
    args_ok = (1, "test1")
    args_err = (2, None)
    
    try:
        cur.execute(sql, args_ok)
        print(True)
    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
        print(False)
    
    try:
        cur.execute(sql, args_err)
        print(True)
    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
        print(False)
    
    conn.commit()

    cur.execute('DELETE FROM test_insert')
    conn.commit()
    
    cur.execute('DROP TABLE test_insert')
    conn.close()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

<?php
try {
try { $cls = new Dom\NamedNodeMap(); } catch (\Throwable $_e) { $cls = new stdClass(); }
try { $clsAttr=$cls->length; } catch (\Throwable $_e) {}
/*
  Testing fgetcsv() to read from a file when provided with the length argument
  value less than the line size
*/
echo "*** Testing fgetcsv() : with length less than line size ***\n";
/* the array is with three elements in it. Each element should be read as
   1st element is delimiter, 2nd element is enclosure
   and 3rd element is csv fields
*/
$csv_lists = array (
  array(',', '"', '"water",fruit'),
  array(',', '"', '"water","fruit"'),
  array(' ', '^', '^water^ ^fruit^'),
  array(':', '&', '&water&:&fruit&'),
  array('=', '=', '=water===fruit='),
  array('-', '-', '-water--fruit-air'),
  array('-', '-', '-water---fruit---air-'),
  array(':', '&', '&""""&:&"&:,:":&,&:,,,,')
);
$filename = __DIR__ . '/fgetcsv_variation6.tmp';
@unlink($filename);
$file_modes = array ("r","rb", "rt", "r+", "r+b", "r+t",
                     "a+", "a+b", "a+t",
                     "w+", "w+b", "w+t",
                     "x+", "x+b", "x+t");
$loop_counter = 1;
foreach ($csv_lists as $csv_list) {
  for($mode_counter = 0; $mode_counter < count($file_modes); $mode_counter++) {
    // create the file and add the content with has csv fields
    if ( strstr($file_modes[$mode_counter], "r") ) {
      $file_handle = fopen($filename, "w");
    } else {
      $file_handle = fopen($filename, $file_modes[$mode_counter] );
    }
    if ( !$file_handle ) {
      echo "Error: failed to create file $filename!\n";
      exit();
    }
    $delimiter = $csv_list[0];
    $enclosure = $csv_list[1];
    $csv_field = $csv_list[2];
    fwrite($file_handle, $csv_field . "\n");
    // write another line of text and a blank line
    // this will be used to test, if the fgetcsv() read more than a line and its
    // working when only a blan line is read
    fwrite($file_handle, "This is line of text without csv fields\n");
    fwrite($file_handle, "\n"); // blank line
    // close the file if the mode to be used is read mode  and re-open using read mode
    // else rewind the file pointer to beginning of the file
    if ( strstr($file_modes[$mode_counter], "r" ) ) {
      fclose($file_handle);
      $file_handle = fopen($filename, $file_modes[$mode_counter]);
    } else {
      // rewind the file pointer to bof
      rewind($file_handle);
    }
    echo "\n-- Testing fgetcsv() with file opened using $file_modes[$mode_counter] mode --\n";
    // call fgetcsv() to parse csv fields
    // use length as less than the actual size of the line
    fseek($file_handle, 0, SEEK_SET);
    var_dump( fgetcsv($file_handle, 9, $delimiter, $enclosure, escape: "\\") );
    // check the file pointer position and if eof
    var_dump( ftell($file_handle) );
    var_dump( feof($file_handle) );
    // read rest of the line
    var_dump( fgetcsv($file_handle, 1024, $delimiter, $enclosure, escape: "\\") );
    // check the file pointer position and if eof
    var_dump( ftell($file_handle) );
    var_dump( feof($file_handle) );
    // close the file
    fclose($file_handle);
    //delete file
    unlink($filename);
  } //end of mode loop
} // end of foreach
echo "Done\n";
$fusion = $mode_counter;
$fusion = include __DIR__ . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'browsernames.inc';
echo "*** Testing get_browser() : error functionality ***\n";
/* Unknown browser uses defaults. */
var_dump( get_browser( 'foobar', true ) );
/* Some wrong parameters, no HTTP_USER_AGENT set */
var_dump( get_browser( null, 'foobar' ) );
var_dump(get_defined_vars());

<?php
/*
  Testing fgetcsv() to read from a file when provided with the length argument
  value less than the line size
*/

echo "*** Testing fgetcsv() : with length less than line size ***\n";

/* the array is with three elements in it. Each element should be read as
   1st element is delimiter, 2nd element is enclosure
   and 3rd element is csv fields
*/
$csv_lists = array (
  array(',', '"', '"water",fruit'),
  array(',', '"', '"water","fruit"'),
  array(' ', '^', '^water^ ^fruit^'),
  array(':', '&', '&water&:&fruit&'),
  array('=', '=', '=water===fruit='),
  array('-', '-', '-water--fruit-air'),
  array('-', '-', '-water---fruit---air-'),
  array(':', '&', '&""""&:&"&:,:":&,&:,,,,')
);

$filename = __DIR__ . '/fgetcsv_variation6.tmp';
@unlink($filename);

$file_modes = array ("r","rb", "rt", "r+", "r+b", "r+t",
                     "a+", "a+b", "a+t",
                     "w+", "w+b", "w+t",
                     "x+", "x+b", "x+t");

$loop_counter = 1;
foreach ($csv_lists as $csv_list) {
  for($mode_counter = 0; $mode_counter < count($file_modes); $mode_counter++) {
    // create the file and add the content with has csv fields
    if ( strstr($file_modes[$mode_counter], "r") ) {
      $file_handle = fopen($filename, "w");
    } else {
      $file_handle = fopen($filename, $file_modes[$mode_counter] );
    }
    if ( !$file_handle ) {
      echo "Error: failed to create file $filename!\n";
      exit();
    }
    $delimiter = $csv_list[0];
    $enclosure = $csv_list[1];
    $csv_field = $csv_list[2];
    fwrite($file_handle, $csv_field . "\n");
    // write another line of text and a blank line
    // this will be used to test, if the fgetcsv() read more than a line and its
    // working when only a blan line is read
    fwrite($file_handle, "This is line of text without csv fields\n");
    fwrite($file_handle, "\n"); // blank line

    // close the file if the mode to be used is read mode  and re-open using read mode
    // else rewind the file pointer to beginning of the file
    if ( strstr($file_modes[$mode_counter], "r" ) ) {
      fclose($file_handle);
      $file_handle = fopen($filename, $file_modes[$mode_counter]);
    } else {
      // rewind the file pointer to bof
      rewind($file_handle);
    }

    echo "\n-- Testing fgetcsv() with file opened using $file_modes[$mode_counter] mode --\n";

    // call fgetcsv() to parse csv fields

    // use length as less than the actual size of the line
    fseek($file_handle, 0, SEEK_SET);
    var_dump( fgetcsv($file_handle, 9, $delimiter, $enclosure, escape: "\\") );
    // check the file pointer position and if eof
    var_dump( ftell($file_handle) );
    var_dump( feof($file_handle) );
    // read rest of the line
    var_dump( fgetcsv($file_handle, 1024, $delimiter, $enclosure, escape: "\\") );
    // check the file pointer position and if eof
    var_dump( ftell($file_handle) );
    var_dump( feof($file_handle) );

    // close the file
    fclose($file_handle);
    //delete file
    unlink($filename);
  } //end of mode loop
} // end of foreach

echo "Done\n";
?>

<?php

#[AllowDynamicProperties]
class Node {
    public $next;
    // forcing dynamic property creation is key
}

$first = new Node();
$first->previous = $first;
$first->next = $first;

$cur = $first;

for ($i = 0; $i < 50000; $i++) {
    $new = new Node();
    $new->previous = $cur;
    $cur->next = $new;
    $new->next = $first;
    $first->previous = $new;
    $cur = $new;
}

try {
	// Force comparison manually to trigger zend_hash_compare
	$first == $cur;
} catch(Error $e) {
	echo $e->getMessage(). PHP_EOL;
}
?>

            $asyncLoopResult = 'FAILURE';

<?php

function printable($s) {
    $result = '';
    for ($i = 0; $i < strlen($s); $i++) {
        $ch = $s[$i];
        if (ord($ch) <= 32 || ord($ch) >= 128) {
            $result .= '(' . ord($ch) . ')';
        } else {
            $result .= $ch;
        }
    }
    return $result;
}

function randStr() {
    $sz = rand(0, 20);
    $buf = '';
    for ($i = 0; $i < $sz; $i++) {
        $what = rand(0, 19);
        switch ($what) {
            case 0: $buf .= "\r"; break;
            case 1: $buf .= "\n"; break;
            case 2: $buf .= "\t"; break;
            case 3: $buf .= "\f"; break;
            case 4: $buf .= ' '; break;
            case 5: $buf .= ','; break;
            case 6: $buf .= '"'; break;
            case 7: $buf .= "'"; break;
            case 8: $buf .= "\\"; break;
            default: $buf .= chr(rand(0, 299)); break;
        }
    }
    return $buf;
}

function doRandom($iter) {
    for ($i = 0; $i < $iter; $i++) {
        $nLines = rand(1, 4);
        $nCol = rand(1, 3);
        $lines = [];
        for ($j = 0; $j < $nLines; $j++) {
            $line = [];
            for ($k = 0; $k < $nCol; $k++) {
                $line[] = randStr();
            }
            $lines[] = $line;
        }
        $result = '';
        foreach ($lines as $line) {
            $result .= implode(',', array_map(function($v) {
                return '"' . str_replace('"', '""', $v) . '"';
            }, $line)) . "\n";
        }
        $parseResult = explode("\n", trim($result));
        foreach ($lines as $i => $line) {
            $parsedLine = explode(',', $parseResult[$i]);
            for ($j = 0; $j < count($line); $j++) {
                if ($line[$j] !== trim($parsedLine[$j], '"')) {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

$iter = 10000;
doRandom($iter);

?>
